claims.claim: 8 -> 11 zero-day exploits a month, 2025 average vs 2026; 22 in August 2026

claims.claim: resold LLM API access, with single-day fraudulent charges above $100,000

claims.claim: GTIG's own detection list is plain: unexpected service-account creation, bursts of LLM API calls from odd IPs, and unreviewed edits to coding-assistant files such as .claude/settings.json
claims.quote: Threat actors created unauthorized IAM and service accounts or attached administrative policies to service roles. / The botnet or proxy service generated millions of LLM API calls in approximately 24 hours before the credentials were revoked. / modifying .claude/settings.json configuration files so that when users started up Claude Code, it would automatically trigger the download of the SOMBERMEME backdoor.
claims.fix: The page has no detection list. These three items are observed attacker behaviours. The only defender content is Google SecOps ARTEX rulepacks and a linked Mandiant hardening guide. Say 'GTIG describes attackers creating service accounts, running bursts of LLM API calls and editing .claude/settings.json' and frame the detection advice as the brief's own inference. Also 'from odd IPs' and 'unreviewed edits' are not in the page.
